customManagers.description: Bump the pinned uv version in any workflow (root + template body)

Track `.ruff-version`, the single place this repo records a ruff version — read by ci.yml's repo-lint job, by the PostToolUse format hook (.claude/hooks/ruff-format.sh) and by scripts/micro-render-check.py. It replaces an inline `RUFF_VERSION=0.16.0` in ci.yml that carried a `# renovate:` marker and was matched by NOTHING: the workflow customManager above requires a `version: "…"` key, no built-in manager parses a shell assignment inside a `run:` block, and so the pin had been untracked since it was introduced. The file holds exactly one line, so an unanchored version match is unambiguous — Renovate compiles matchStrings without the multiline flag, which makes `^` mean start-of-file rather than start-of-line.

Track the TEMPLATE BODY's Python deps. template/pyproject.toml.jinja is a jinja file, so no built-in manager (pep621/pip_requirements) ever parses it — every lower-bound pin in the template was invisible to Renovate, which is why the dashboard's 'Detected Dependencies' listed no pypi manager at all. Matches a PEP 508 requirement string: name, optional extras (non-capturing, so `uvicorn[standard]` yields depName `uvicorn`), then the `>=` floor. depName allows dots/hyphens (opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi, python-multipart); currentValue is anything up to the closing quote or a comma, so PEP 440 pre-release floors (`>=0.50b0`) and bare majors (`>=7`) are captured too. Jinja-gated lines (`{% if include_admin %}, "itsdangerous>=2.0"`) match like any other because each entry carries its own opening quote.

packageRules.description: Auto-merge every GitHub Actions + pre-commit bump (incl. majors) once the required CI checks pass — the workflow-render gate in .github/workflows/ci.yml makes green real for the template body.

Supply-chain cooldown for every Python dep: never open a PR for a release less than 3 days old. Same posture as SHA-pinning our actions — a compromised or yanked PyPI release is usually caught and pulled within hours, and the template's lower-bound pins mean a bad version would propagate into every generated service's next `uv lock --upgrade`.
Auto-merge Python minor + patch bumps once the required checks are green — the capability matrix locks, syncs, lints, type-checks and tests a real generated project per bump, so green is real.

Python MAJORS are never auto-merged — a major floor bump is a breaking-change review, and it propagates to every downstream service on its next `copier update`. dependencyDashboardApproval holds the PR until a human ticks its box on the Dependency Dashboard.

BOUND THE RUFF-PIN LAG (ledger ticket FMT-2). `.ruff-version` pins the ruff that EDITS code (the PostToolUse format hook) and that two gates run; a capability leg resolves ruff from a fresh `uv lock` against the template's `ruff>=0.15` floor, so the leg always takes whatever is newest at run time and the pin can only ever be BEHIND it. That residual is accepted, not gated: a pin-equals-resolved CI check would red every PR for close to a week on a stale pin, and noise that trains people to ignore red costs more than a bounded lag. This rule is what bounds it — the pin chases the floor in about a day instead of about a week. Three settings, each load-bearing. `minimumReleaseAge: 1 day` shortens the generic 3-day pypi cooldown above (rules merge in order and this one is LAST, so it wins; PREPENDING it would be a silent no-op, with the generic rule overriding it straight back to 3 days). `schedule` is required, not decoration: `minimumReleaseAge` bounds when a release becomes ELIGIBLE, not when Renovate RUNS, and the top-level `schedule:weekly` expands through `schedule:earlyMondays` to `* 0-3 * * 1` — a Monday-04:00-to-Monday-00:00 window — so a 24h cooldown alone still waits for the next Monday and the lag stays ~7 days. `matchUpdateTypes` leaves the major path untouched: a ruff 1.0 still falls through to the major rule above, on dependencyDashboardApproval. Verified against Renovate's own pep440 versioning rather than assumed — 0.16->0.17 and 0.15.22->0.16.0 both classify as `minor`, 0.16->1.0.0 as `major`. Scoped by FILE, not by depName: `template/pyproject.toml.jinja` carries a `ruff>=0.15` floor that the template customManager also reports as depName `ruff`, and that floor SHIPS INTO every generated service, so it keeps the full 3-day supply-chain cooldown. This file does not ship anywhere — it is this repo's own dev tooling, gated by CI on the bump PR itself.
